name: Barbell bench press
setup: Shoulder blades pulled back and down — 'into your back pockets'. Feet flat, driving into the floor.
execution: Elbows roughly under the bar, wrist stacked over elbow. Touch around nipple line. Press slightly back toward the rack.
faults: Shoulder blades letting go mid-set. Elbows flaring to 90° at the bottom. Touching too high on the chest.
shoulder: Keep the touch point low and elbows tucked to about 45°. Never let elbows drift behind the torso line at the bottom. Floor press is the safest variant.

name: Incline machine chest press
setup: Seat height so handles sit at mid-to-lower chest. Shoulder blades back and down against the pad before the first rep.
execution: Press through the full range, controlled lowering to a deep but comfortable stretch. Keep ribs down.
faults: Shoulders rolling forward at lockout. Rushing the lowering phase. Seat too low, pushing the handles upward instead of forward.
shoulder: Stop the lowering where your elbows reach the plane of your torso — don't let them travel behind it. A neutral or semi-neutral grip is safer than a wide pronated one.

name: Pin-loaded machine chest press
setup: Handles level with mid-chest. Back flat against the pad, shoulder blades retracted.
execution: Push through the handles with elbows at about 45°. Full extension without locking hard. Controlled return.
faults: Elbows flaring wide. Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears. Letting the weight stack touch down between reps.
shoulder: Keep elbows from passing the torso line on the return. Neutral grip if the machine offers it.

name: Lying neutral-grip plate-loaded chest press
setup: Lie back, neutral grip, shoulder blades pulled together and down into the pad.
execution: Press straight up, elbows staying at about 45°. Lower under control to a comfortable depth.
faults: Losing scapular retraction at the top. Letting elbows drift wide.
shoulder: This is one of the better pressing options for anterior instability — neutral grip, fixed path. Still stop where elbows reach the torso line.

name: Overhead press
setup: Grip just outside shoulder width. Bar on the front delts, elbows slightly ahead of the bar. Glutes and core braced.
execution: Press up and slightly back. Head moves back as the bar passes, then through so the bar finishes over the crown.
faults: Ribcage flaring and lower back arching. Bar drifting forward. Not finishing with the bar over the head.
shoulder: Overhead work is tolerable for most with anterior instability if the elbows stay in front of the body. Never behind-the-neck. If it pinches at the top, use a landmine press instead.

name: Back squat
setup: Bar on the upper back, hands as close as shoulders allow. Feet about shoulder width, toes slightly out. Big brace.
execution: Break at hips and knees together. Knees track over toes. Depth to at least parallel. Drive up through the mid-foot.
faults: Knees caving in. Weight shifting to the toes. Chest dropping and hips shooting up first.
shoulder: Low-bar position needs shoulder external rotation that may aggravate instability. Use a high-bar position, a wider grip, or the Transformer/safety bar which removes the issue entirely.

name: Transformer bar squat
setup: Pads on the traps, hands on the handles — not gripping hard. Feet set as for a back squat.
execution: Same squat mechanics. The forward-loading pulls you forward; fight it by keeping the chest up and bracing hard.
faults: Letting the bar tip you forward. Using the handles to pull yourself up.
shoulder: The reason to use this bar — no shoulder rotation required. Fully safe for anterior instability.

name: Front squat
setup: Bar across the front delts, elbows high. Clean grip or cross-arm — whichever keeps elbows up.
execution: Stay upright. Knees travel forward and out. Elbows stay high throughout or the bar rolls forward.
faults: Elbows dropping. Rounding the upper back. Hips rising faster than the chest.
shoulder: Clean grip requires wrist and shoulder mobility that may be uncomfortable. Cross-arm or straps on the bar are fine alternatives.

name: Pendulum squat
setup: Feet mid-to-high on the platform. Back flat against the pad. Shoulders under the pads.
execution: Descend as deep as your hips allow without the lower back rounding. Drive through the whole foot.
faults: Lower back lifting off the pad at the bottom. Knees caving. Bouncing out of the hole.

name: Leg press
setup: Feet shoulder width on the platform, mid-height. Back and hips stay on the pad.
execution: Lower until the knees are near 90° or deeper if the hips stay down. Press without locking out hard.
faults: Hips rolling up off the seat at the bottom — the lower back is now loaded. Locking knees. Partial reps with excessive weight.

name: Hack squat
setup: Feet slightly forward on the platform. Back flat on the pad. Shoulders under the pads.
execution: Descend to full depth, knees tracking over toes. Drive through the whole foot.
faults: Heels lifting. Knees caving. Cutting depth as it gets heavy.

name: Deadlift
setup: Bar over mid-foot. Shins touch the bar as you hinge down. Lats set — 'bend the bar around your shins'. Big brace.
execution: Push the floor away. Bar stays in contact with the legs. Hips and shoulders rise together. Finish tall, no lean-back.
faults: Hips shooting up first. Bar drifting away from the shins. Rounding the lower back off the floor. Hyperextending at the top.
shoulder: Fully safe. Arms are straight and at the side. Mixed grip puts one shoulder in external rotation — use double overhand with straps if that bothers you.

name: Trap bar deadlift
setup: Stand centred in the bar. Neutral grip on the handles. Hinge down with a flat back.
execution: More upright than a straight-bar pull — that's expected. Push the floor away and stand tall.
faults: Turning it into a squat with a rounded back. Jerking off the floor.
shoulder: Neutral grip, arms at the sides — nothing here stresses the shoulder.

name: Romanian deadlift
setup: Start standing. Soft bend in the knees that doesn't change through the rep. Lats set, bar close.
execution: Push the hips straight back. Bar slides down the thighs. Stop when the hamstrings stop you — usually just below the knee.
faults: Rounding the lower back to chase range. Bending the knees more as the weight gets heavy. Letting the bar drift forward.
shoulder: Safe. Keep the shoulders pulled slightly back so the bar doesn't drag them forward.

name: Belt squat machine RDL
setup: Belt snug on the hips. Stand tall with a soft knee bend.
execution: Hinge back exactly as a barbell RDL. The load pulls from the hips, not the hands, so the back stays unloaded.
faults: Squatting instead of hinging. Letting the knees drift forward.
shoulder: No shoulder involvement at all. Ideal hinge variant when the shoulder is flared.

name: Weighted roman chair hip hinge
setup: Pad just below the hip crease so the hips can hinge freely. Feet locked in.
execution: Lower by hinging at the hips, flat back throughout. Come up to neutral — not past it into hyperextension.
faults: Rounding the back. Hyperextending at the top. Pad too high, blocking the hinge.

name: Transformer bar hinge
setup: Bar on the back as for a squat. Soft knees.
execution: Push the hips back, chest stays up. Same pattern as a good morning — stop when the hamstrings stop you.
faults: Letting the chest drop and rounding. Bending the knees into a squat.
shoulder: Hands on the handles, no rotation required. Safe.

name: Hip thrust
setup: Upper back on the bench at the bottom of the shoulder blades. Bar across the hips with a pad. Feet so shins are vertical at the top.
execution: Drive through the heels. Chin tucked. Finish with a full hip lockout and a hard glute squeeze — ribs down.
faults: Hyperextending the lower back at the top. Looking up. Feet too far forward.

name: Pull-up
setup: Full dead hang. Shoulder blades slightly engaged — not hanging passively on the joint.
execution: Pull the elbows down and back toward the hips. Chin clears the bar. Lower all the way under control.
faults: Kipping. Not reaching full extension at the bottom. Stopping short of chin over bar.
shoulder: Grip width matters — wider than shoulders pushes toward the at-risk position. Shoulder width or narrower. Neutral grip is safest.

name: Weighted chin-up
setup: Underhand grip at shoulder width. Dead hang with shoulder blades slightly set. Belt snug.
execution: Same pull as a pull-up — elbows to the hips. Biceps naturally contribute more. Full range every rep.
faults: Half reps at the bottom. Swinging the belt weight. Hunching forward at the top.
shoulder: The underhand grip keeps the shoulder in a safer position than a wide pronated pull-up. Well suited to anterior instability — your goal lift is a good choice.

name: Lat pulldown
setup: Thighs locked under the pad. Grip just wider than shoulders. Slight lean back, chest up.
execution: Pull the elbows down and back — think of driving them into your back pockets. Bar to the upper chest. Controlled return to a full stretch.
faults: Leaning back and rowing it. Pulling behind the neck. Cutting the top of the range.
shoulder: Never behind the neck. Keep the grip at or slightly wider than shoulders — very wide grips move toward the at-risk position.

name: Underhand plate-loaded lat pulldown
setup: Underhand grip at shoulder width. Thighs locked in. Chest tall.
execution: Pull elbows down and in to the sides. Squeeze at the bottom. Let the arms fully extend at the top for the stretch.
faults: Curling the handles with the arms instead of driving the elbows. Rounding forward.
shoulder: Supinated grip is the shoulder-friendly option. Safe.

name: Single-arm plate lat pulldown
setup: Brace the free hand on the machine. Chest up, slight lean toward the working side.
execution: Pull the elbow to the hip. Let the shoulder blade rotate up and out at the top for the full stretch.
faults: Twisting the torso to cheat the weight. Shrugging at the top.
shoulder: Neutral grip, arm travelling in front of the body. Safe.

name: Seated cable row
setup: Feet braced, slight knee bend. Chest up, upright torso.
execution: Pull the handle to the lower chest, squeeze the shoulder blades together. Let them separate fully on the return.
faults: Leaning back to move the weight. Shrugging. Rounding forward on the return.
shoulder: Neutral grip, elbows close. Safe.

name: Seated single-arm cable row
setup: Square the hips. Free hand braced. Chest tall.
execution: Row the elbow to the hip, letting the shoulder blade pull back fully. Full stretch forward on the return.
faults: Rotating the torso. Shrugging the working shoulder.
shoulder: Safe — arm travels close to the body.

name: Face pull
setup: Rope at face height or slightly above. Step back for tension. Stand tall.
execution: Pull toward the forehead, elbows high and wide, finishing with the hands rotating back — the external rotation is the point.
faults: Pulling to the chest like a row. Skipping the rotation at the end. Using too much weight.
shoulder: The end position is external rotation at 90° abduction — the at-risk angle. Lower the pulley to chest height and finish the pull lower. Light loads only.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
setup: Slight forward lean. Dumbbells at the sides, slight bend in the elbows.
execution: Lead with the elbows, not the hands. Raise to about shoulder height. Think of pouring water out of a jug at the top.
faults: Swinging. Shrugging. Going above shoulder height — that's traps now.
shoulder: Raise in the scapular plane — about 30° forward of straight sideways. Pure side-plane raising with a thumbs-down position is the position to avoid.

name: Standing machine lateral raise
setup: Pads against the forearms or hands, depending on machine. Stand tall.
execution: Raise with the elbows to shoulder height. Pause briefly. Lower under control.
faults: Shrugging. Rushing. Leaning back to cheat the last reps.
shoulder: Most machines arc in the scapular plane, which is good. Stop at shoulder height.

name: Seated machine lateral raise
setup: Seat so the pivot aligns with the shoulder joint. Pads just above the elbows.
execution: Drive the elbows up and out to shoulder height. Controlled return.
faults: Pivot misaligned, causing the arms to rise unevenly. Shrugging.
shoulder: Stop at shoulder height. Fine for instability.

name: Machine rear delt fly
setup: Chest against the pad. Handles at shoulder height. Arms slightly bent.
execution: Drive the elbows back and out, squeezing the rear delts. Don't retract the shoulder blades — that's upper back.
faults: Rowing it with the shoulder blades. Using momentum. Over-extending past the body line.
shoulder: Stop when the elbows reach the plane of the torso. Don't drive past it.

name: Sideways single-arm machine rear delt fly
setup: Sit sideways, working arm on the handle. Brace with the other hand.
execution: Sweep the arm back in an arc, elbow slightly bent. Squeeze. Return under control.
faults: Rotating the torso. Swinging.
shoulder: Stop at the body line — don't pull the arm behind the torso.

name: Seated overhand DB rear delt fly
setup: Bent over on a bench, chest near the thighs. Dumbbells hanging, slight elbow bend.
execution: Raise out to the sides, leading with the elbows. Pinkies slightly up. Pause at the top.
faults: Swinging. Squeezing the shoulder blades instead of the rear delts. Too heavy.
shoulder: Light weight only. Stop at the plane of the torso.

name: Cable pushdown
setup: Elbows pinned at the sides. Slight forward lean. Handle at chest height to start.
execution: Extend fully at the bottom without the elbows moving. Control the return until the forearms pass parallel.
faults: Elbows drifting forward and back. Leaning over the weight. Shortening the range as it gets heavy.

name: Cable rope pushdown
setup: Rope at chest height. Elbows tucked, slight lean.
execution: Push down and spread the rope apart at the bottom. Full extension. Controlled return.
faults: Elbows flaring out. Using the shoulders to push.

name: Overhead tricep extension machine
setup: Upper arms against the pad, pointing up. Elbows aligned with the pivot.
execution: Extend fully. Lower until you feel the triceps stretch — this is where the growth is.
faults: Upper arms drifting forward off the pad. Cutting the stretch at the bottom.
shoulder: Overhead position is generally tolerable because the arm is in flexion, not abduction. If it pinches, use a pushdown instead.

name: Seated pin-loaded machine triceps dip
setup: Handles at chest height. Shoulders down, chest up.
execution: Press down through the handles to full extension. Control the return — don't let the shoulders rise.
faults: Shrugging the shoulders up. Leaning forward to use the chest. Partial range.
shoulder: Far safer than a free dip. Stop the return before the elbows pass the torso line.

name: Weighted dip
setup: Arms locked, slight forward lean. Shoulders depressed.
execution: Lower until the upper arm is parallel. Press back up. Keep the lean consistent.
faults: Going too deep. Shoulders rolling forward at the bottom. Flaring the elbows.
shoulder: The bottom of a deep dip loads the front of the shoulder heavily. For anterior instability: shallow depth only, or replace with the machine dip.

name: Pin-loaded machine preacher curl
setup: Armpits over the pad edge. Elbows aligned with the machine pivot.
execution: Curl through the full range. Lower slowly — don't drop into the stretched position.
faults: Shoulders rising off the pad. Bouncing at the bottom. Cutting the lowering phase short.

name: Single-arm cable biceps curl
setup: Elbow pinned at the side. Slight step back for constant tension.
execution: Curl with the elbow fixed. Full squeeze at the top. Controlled lowering to full extension.
faults: Elbow drifting forward. Swinging the torso. Stopping short of full extension.

name: Nordic hamstring curl
setup: Knees on a pad, ankles anchored. Hips extended — body in one straight line.
execution: Lower as slowly as possible by letting the knees extend. Catch with the hands only when the hamstrings give out.
faults: Bending at the hips. Dropping instead of resisting. Expecting to do the full range early.

name: Lying leg curl
setup: Pad just above the heels. Hips pressed into the bench. Toes pointed toward the shins.
execution: Curl to full contraction. Lower under control — the stretch matters as much as the squeeze.
faults: Hips rising off the pad. Pointing the toes, which recruits the calves. Dropping the weight.

name: Leg extension
setup: Knees aligned with the machine pivot. Pad on the lower shin. Back against the seat.
execution: Extend to a full lockout and pause. Lower under control through the full range.
faults: Kicking the weight up. Partial range. Lifting the hips off the seat.

name: Standing machine calf raise
setup: Balls of the feet on the edge. Heels dropped below for the stretch. Knees straight but not locked.
execution: Full stretch at the bottom, pause. Drive to the top, pause. Slow throughout.
faults: Bouncing. Bending the knees to bounce out of the stretch. Half reps.

name: Seated plate-loaded machine calf raise
setup: Pad on the lower thigh. Balls of the feet on the edge, heels low.
execution: Same tempo — stretch, pause, drive, pause. This hits the soleus; expect to go lighter than standing.
faults: Bouncing. Rushing the bottom position.

name: Multi-hip machine hip abduction
setup: Pad against the outside of the thigh. Stand tall, hold the rail.
execution: Drive the leg out to the side. Pause. Return under control without letting the stack rest.
faults: Leaning away to cheat. Swinging. Using the torso.

name: Seated machine hip adduction
setup: Pads inside the knees. Start wider than comfortable for the stretch.
execution: Squeeze together through the full range. Pause. Open slowly.
faults: Pulsing short reps. Letting the stack drop open.

name: Captain's chair straight leg raise
setup: Forearms on the pads, back against the pad. Shoulders down.
execution: Raise the legs by curling the pelvis up, not just lifting the thighs. Lower slowly.
faults: Swinging. Lifting with the hip flexors only — no pelvic tilt. Shrugging into the pads.

name: T-bar row
setup: Chest over the bar, hinged to about 45°. Flat back, lats set.
execution: Row the handle to the lower chest. Elbows stay fairly close. Squeeze, lower under control.
faults: Heaving with the lower back. Torso rising with each rep. Flaring elbows wide.
shoulder: Elbows close to the body — flaring wide moves toward horizontal abduction. Safe when done tight.

name: Chest-supported row
setup: Chest fully on the pad. Feet braced. Arms hanging straight.
execution: Row the elbows back and down. Squeeze the shoulder blades. Let them separate fully on the return.
faults: Lifting the chest off the pad. Shrugging. Short range at the bottom.
shoulder: The best row for a bad shoulder — the pad removes any need to brace with the torso. Keep elbows close.
